tools.name: securityCheck
tools.title: Security Check
tools.fields: [operation:"package", ecosystem*, packageName*, mainGoal?, reasoning?, release?, version?, …] | [operation:"url", url*, mainGoal?, reasoning?, view?] | [operation:"advisory", id*, mainGoal?, reasoning?, repo?, view?] | [operation:"commit", commit*, mainGoal?, reasoning?, repo?, view?] | [operation:"repository", repo*, mainGoal?, reasoning?, view?]
tools.help:
Examples:
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"package","ecosystem":"npm","packageName":"lodash","version":"4.17.20"}]}'
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"url","url":"https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash"}]}'
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"advisory","id":"GHSA-29mw-wpgm-hmr9"}]}'
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"commit","commit":"6879efc2c1596d11a6a6ad296f80063b558d5e0f"}]}'
  octocode securityCheck '{"queries":[{"operation":"repository","repo":"tmcw/leftpad"}]}'

Input: {"queries":[…]} for fresh calls, optionally with "responseChars" (page size target; the rest pages, nothing dropped); copy {"cursor":"…"} from a continuation.

Required fields, by operation:
  package     operation, ecosystem, packageName
  url         operation, url
  advisory    operation, id
  commit      operation, commit
  repository  operation, repo

Each form's example: octocode schema securityCheck --view variants

Fields: octocode schema securityCheck

output.warnings: Notes for the whole response; each applies to every row.
output.oversized: This response holds an indivisible value longer than responseChars; nothing is cut. Fixed envelope parts, repeated context and responsePagination may exceed the target without this flag. Per-call metadata (rateLimit, clientWaits, observedAt) and rejected queries are not counted.
output.responsePagination: Reads on when next is present: preserve every row part and run next until none remains. Expired saved work fails explicitly.
output.responsePagination.hasMore: true: next reads more of this request.
output.responsePagination.next: The rest of this request, one call for every row's walk; run unchanged. Rows keep their query's index.
output.responsePagination.replayed: Reads saved output without acquisition or inference; any usage in the output is historical.
output.commitSha: The resolved source commit for this result.
output.retryable: On a transient row: true = a retry can succeed, false = it cannot.
output.ssoUrl: GitHub SAML SSO authorization URL (x-github-sso) for a 403 whose token must be authorized for the org; open it, then retry.
output.clientWaits: Waits this row spent on the client before its provider requests, by kind: latency the provider did not cause.
output.observedAt: ISO time of the saved answer reused here: its origin was not asked again, so later changes are not shown.
output.rateLimit: The provider's rate limit behind a failure: when a retry can run.
output.rateLimit.resource: The provider's limit bucket, e.g. core or search.
output.hints: Optional guidance for empty results or errors. Evidence and coverage disclosures use warnings; executable follow-ups use objects. Related calls never complete a partial result.
output.next: Pagination and coverage continuations: the rest of this result (a paged response's walks ride responsePagination.next). Follow each unchanged; they are authoritative even when pagination.hasMore is false. Only this field, never hints, may satisfy isPartial.
output.pagination: Row-local pagination summary. Inspect data.next, partialReasons, and terminalLimit for completeness.
output.pagination.unit: What offset, length and total count: items (list rows), files, matches (astSearch matches, localSearch matchOnly occurrences), lines (localSearch hit rows: a matched line, or each hit window of a long line; a body's lines), bytes or chars.
output.pagination.offset: Where this page starts in unit, from 0. A bytes window counts the text as served: decoded (a BOM dropped, UTF-16 as UTF-8), each redaction placeholder as the bytes it shows, so it can differ from the file's bytes.
output.pagination.length: How many units this page holds.
output.pagination.total: Size of the whole list or body in unit; absent when unknown. A read counts what it selects (its ranges, matches or transformed view), not the file: data.totalLines counts the file, and a lines window states total only when it differs.
output.pagination.countScope: How much total counts: absent or complete, all of it; loaded, the part read so far; partial, what was readable; capped, up to the provider's result cap. Anything but complete makes total a floor.
output.pagination.hasMore: true: next.nextPage here or on the row, or responsePagination.next, reads the rest. false: this list or body is read to its end, not a guarantee that no other continuation exists.
output.pagination.oversized: A bytes or chars window shows an indivisible redaction marker whole: its text is wider than length, cut short of the marker, or empty when the marker belongs to the next window. Offsets stay nominal; walking on still reads every unit once.
output.isPartial: True when this row does not cover the requested scope for a reason pagination does not already state; more pages show as hasMore with next.* or responsePagination.next, not as isPartial. Inspect next, partialReasons, warnings, and terminalLimit.
output.terminalLimit: True when a provider or runtime limit leaves part of the requested scope unreachable by any call; report that scope. A next call still reads the rest, so keep walking.
output.partialReasons: Machine-readable reasons this row has incomplete coverage.
output.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error means nothing was judged. reason explains a gap, and next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete.
output.answer: The result in one sentence of typed values, with no text from a source: the target, whether it is affected, what to upgrade to, which CVEs. view summary states it only where no field does: an advisory's ranges, or why a target has no verdict.
output.affected: true: OSV matched this target. false: none known to OSV at this version, which proves only that. Absent: not known, as for a version not evaluated or an empty commit.
output.upgradeTo: The lowest fixed version clearing every listed advisory, checked with OSV at that version.
output.advisoryCount: view summary: advisories counted for the target, withdrawn ones left out. Absent: not checked, or the walk has not ended.
output.highestSeverity: view summary: the most severe label among the counted advisories, as their databases word it. Absent: none states one.
output.unfixedInMajorCount: view summary: counted advisories no release of version's own major is listed as fixing, so upgradeTo is in a later major. Absent: none.
output.link: view summary: the record of the most severe counted advisory.
output.upgradeNote: Why no upgrade is named, or what OSV lists at upgradeTo besides.
output.packageName: The public registry's name for the package, as sent to OSV.
output.version: The exact version the registry confirmed; every advisory is OSV's match for it.
output.registryConfirmed: No registry reader exists for this ecosystem, so name and version were not confirmed: OSV matched the text sent, and a misspelled name reads as none known.
output.latestVersion: The registry's latest stable version: view details states it, view summary when outdated is true. Absent there: the registry read failed or has no such notion.
output.latestPublishedAt: When latestVersion was published, as YYYY-MM-DD.
output.currentPublishedAt: When version was published, as YYYY-MM-DD.
output.isLatest: version equals latestVersion. Absent: either is unknown.
output.outdated: A newer release exists, published after version. Absent: not known; false is not safe.
output.upgradeKind: What moving to latestVersion changes, compared as plain dotted numbers; unknown otherwise, never guessed.
output.cautions: Signals to review before relying on this target, each with its raw values. lowTraction alone is a note. Absent: none fired, or trust was not evaluated: see repository and sources.
output.cautions[].level: review: look before relying on it. note: context only.
output.cautions[].rule: lowTraction: The repository has fewer than 100 stars. unmaintained: No push to the repository for more than 365 days. archived: The repository is archived: read-only, no fixes will land. deprecated: The registry marks this version or package deprecated. yanked: The registry yanked or retracted this version. repositoryMissing: The repository the registry names does not exist. repositoryMoved: The repository the registry names moved or was renamed. noSourceRepo: The registry names no source repository; trust was not evaluated. commitNotInRepository: GitHub has no such commit in the repository. onlyInForkNetwork: The commit resolves through the repository but is the head of no branch, the tip of no tag, in no pull request and in the history of no branch or tag: it may live only in a fork. malware: A source reports malicious code in this package: GitHub's advisory database classes a record as malware, or OSV lists a malicious-packages report (MAL-); on a package row, at the version asked. why names each.
output.cautions[].basis: reported: a source states it. heuristic: a threshold in policy inferred it.
output.cautions[].why: The raw values, the threshold and today's date, as typed facts.
output.repository: The source repository GitHub described: package rows, commit with repo, and the repository operation. Absent: none named or GitHub unread: see sources.
output.repository.name: Repository name without owner.
output.repository.pushedAt: Last push to any branch, as YYYY-MM-DD; never updated_at, which an archive or a star can move.
output.repository.provenance: How the package's link to this repository is established. claimed: the registry says so. verified: a signed attestation or a matching tag proves it. A claimed repository can add a caution, never clear one.
output.repository.namedBy: The latest release names this repository; the version's own is not on GitHub (cautions name both).
output.repository.observedAt: The day these facts were read.
output.versionEvaluated: The requested version is not on the public registry, so OSV was asked about the package only: read each advisory's affected ranges.
output.sources: Each source asked; view summary lists only one that failed, stopped early or does not cover the target. A failed source leaves the row partial (sourceFailed), never clean; the row keeps what the others answered. A resumed page whose OSV read fails is an error.
output.sources[].status: found: it holds advisories for the target. noneKnown: a finished walk found none, which proves only that source; GitHub describing a target it holds none for is noneKnown, its description in repository or facts. partial: it stopped early; next.nextPage reads on. failed: it was asked and did not answer, never clean. unavailable: not asked, for want of a token or quota. notCovered: it does not cover this target, as a repository off GitHub. Statuses are independent per source: github noneKnown beside osv found is consistent.
output.sources[].facts: What this source stated of the target.
output.sources[].facts.exists: GitHub has this commit in the repository.
output.sources[].facts.signature: GitHub's verification of the commit; unverified is a note, not a finding.
output.sources[].facts.heads: Branches whose head is this commit; absent: not read.
output.sources[].facts.pulls: Pull requests that contain this commit; absent: not read.
output.sources[].facts.onDefaultBranch: The default branch's history holds this commit; absent: not read.
output.sources[].facts.inBranch: Branches whose history holds this commit, read only when no head, pull request, tag or default branch holds it; complete only when inRefsComplete is true.
output.sources[].facts.inTag: Tags that point at this commit; when none does and nothing else holds it, the tags whose history holds it, complete only when inRefsComplete is true. Absent: not read.
output.sources[].facts.inRefsComplete: With inBranch or inTag from history: true when every branch and tag was compared; false when the walk ended at the page that found a holder or a comparison failed, so other refs may hold it too.
output.sources[].facts.repositoryAdvisories: Ids of the repository's published advisories that OSV does not list for this commit or version (a package row: those naming the package whose own range does not exclude the version): the repository's word, not counted in answer; the repository operation reads each with its ranges. Partial when why names an advisory stop.
output.sources[].facts.globalAdvisories: Ids of GitHub's reviewed advisories that GitHub matches to this version and OSV does not list: GitHub's word, not counted in answer; the advisory operation reads each.
output.sources[].errorCode: Why failed or unavailable: the source's own refusal, such as a rate limit.
output.sources[].why: What to do about it, as the sign-in or the quota reset time.
output.sources[].anonymous: GitHub was read without a token: public data only, under the anonymous rate limit, so a private repository or advisory reads as missing. Sign in to read them.
output.advisories: view details: one row per source record, once every source finished. Records sharing an id remain separate; no field is inherited from another record. An omitted collection within a record means no selected items stated there, without distinguishing an absent upstream field from an empty array. view summary: the advisory operation alone lists them, one row per advisory (id, aliases, severity, summary, fixedIn, link). []: a finished check found none known to OSV, a floor rather than proof. Absent: not checked.
output.advisories[].link: The provider's advisory page. Absent when `source` is the same address.
output.advisories[].source: One source-record location reported by the provider; affected metadata retains each entry's source locations and attribution.
output.advisories[].githubType: GitHub's class of the record: unreviewed, GitHub has not checked it; malware, the package itself is malicious. Absent: not GitHub's database, or it states none.
output.advisories[].publisher: The GitHub account that published a repository advisory.
output.advisories[].credits: Who the source credits, with GitHub's credit type.
output.advisories[].severity: The database's own label, lowercased; absent when it gave none.
output.advisories[].cvss: CVSS as each source published it.
output.advisories[].cvss[].score: The base score the source publishes with the vector, as GitHub does; absent: it gives the vector only, as OSV does. Never computed here.
output.advisories[].epss: GitHub's EPSS for the advisory; absent: GitHub states none, or its record was not read.
output.advisories[].epss.percentage: Probability of exploitation in the next 30 days.
output.advisories[].epss.percentile: Share of scored CVEs with this probability or less.
output.advisories[].fixedIn: Fix versions only. A package row with a version lists the one fix for that version's line; the advisory read lists every fixed version, one per affected range in OSV order; upgradeTo is the one that clears the queried version. Omitted when this record's own affected ranges already state every selected fix, or when none is stated; never proof of no fix. A version is safe only outside every affected range.
output.advisories[].withdrawn: When the advisory was withdrawn: retracted, not a finding. An advisory's records (aliases) count as withdrawn only when every record is.
output.advisories[].alsoAffects: Other packages this record names; link holds their ranges.
output.advisories[].disputedBy: Aliases another database keeps for this package that OSV does not list at this version: the databases disagree. The row still counts it, as OSV lists it; read each record's ranges.
output.advisories[].affected: The selected affected entries with the package identity each source states. A package query selects its own entries; an advisory query includes every entry.
output.advisories[].affected[].ecosystem: The package ecosystem, including any distribution release suffix. GitHub names use the contract's OSV mapping.
output.advisories[].affected[].purl: Package URL exactly as the source states it, including any version, qualifiers or subpath. Absent when the source states none.
output.advisories[].affected[].ecosystemSpecifi: This entry's ecosystem-specific metadata, including source keys as supplied.
output.advisories[].affected[].databaseSpecific: This entry's database-specific metadata, including source keys and range statements as supplied.
output.advisories[].references: This provider's selected references, preserving their order and types. Omitted: no selected items stated in this record. Never inherited from another record.

output.moduleOnly.advisories[].disputedBy: Aliases another database keeps for this package that OSV does not list at this version: the databases disagree. The row still counts it, as OSV lists it; read each record's ranges.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected: The selected affected entries with the package identity each source states. A package query selects its own entries; an advisory query includes every entry.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected[].ecosy: The package ecosystem, including any distribution release suffix. GitHub names use the contract's OSV mapping.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected[].purl: Package URL exactly as the source states it, including any version, qualifiers or subpath. Absent when the source states none.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected[].ecosy: This entry's ecosystem-specific metadata, including source keys as supplied.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].affected[].datab: This entry's database-specific metadata, including source keys and range statements as supplied.
output.moduleOnly.advisories[].references: This provider's selected references, preserving their order and types. Omitted: no selected items stated in this record. Never inherited from another record.
output.results[].status: Absent: evidence. outOfRange: a page past the end; pagination.total states the size (next.restart).
output.results[].rowPart: This row spans response pages; concatenate its parts in order.
output.results[].rowPart.continues: The innermost array element this part continues; pointer indexes are the joined row's, and each element on the pointer path also continues.
output.results[].rowPart.continues.array: JSON pointer of the array this part resumes.
output.results[].rowPart.text: JSON pointer, in the joined row's indexes, of the string this part continues: append this part's value there to the previous part's.
output.error: Why the whole call was rejected.

query.name: securityCheck
query.description:
<when>Use to check a package version, purl, URL, advisory id (CVE, GHSA), commit or GitHub repo for known vulnerabilities and fixes. Package to repo mapping: artifactSearch.</when>
Example: {"queries":[{"operation":"package","ecosystem":"npm","packageName":"lodash","version":"4.17.20"}]}
Queries OSV: no private commits (hash is sent). Names are registry-confirmed when supported, otherwise sent as given.
advisoryCount 0: none known, not safe. error: not checked. A caution is no verdict.
